## 🚀 Flagship Case Studies

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.card .h-100 .shadow-sm}
::: {.card-body}
<h3 class="card-title">Verifying a Published Hypertension Markov Model</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Cost-effectiveness of two antihypertensive regimens in China — Feng et al. 2023 (<em>J Int Med Res</em>, CC BY-NC)</h6>
<p class="card-text">A four-state Markov cost-effectiveness model rebuilt in R from the published inputs and checked stage by stage against the TECH-VER verification checklist. The published QALYs reproduce exactly and both arms' costs reconcile — the amlodipine arm only once its drug price is taken from the paper's own Figure 4 rather than its Table 2, which differ by 35 CNY a year. The trial percentages behind the transition matrix are cumulative over a 36-month follow-up and are used as one-year probabilities: run the model over the trial's own three years and it returns 11.2% cumulative death where 4.1% went in. Correcting that halves the health gain, and the direction of the published conclusion survives while its magnitudes do not.</p>
<a href="./11_Hypertension_Markov_QC_Replication/01_Hypertension_Markov_Replication.qmd" class="stretched-link">View the verification &rarr;</a>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.card .h-100 .shadow-sm}
::: {.card-body}
<h3 class="card-title">Replicating a Published Multinomial NMA</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Response rates in relapsed/refractory myeloma — van Beurden-Tan et al. 2022 (<em>BMC Cancer</em>, CC-BY)</h6>
<p class="card-text">A Bayesian multinomial network meta-analysis over 17 phase III trials and 16 treatments, rebuilt in Stan from the published trial counts and cross-checked by running the original WinBUGS code in JAGS. All sixteen response rates reconcile to within 0.27 percentage points and SUCRA to within 0.2 — but only after correcting the data file the paper supplies for replication, which produces an error of 19.6 points as published. The rebuild then asks what the ranking rests on: the treatment reported as best holds 47% of the posterior probability of being best, and loses that place when an undiscussed continuity constant or the prior width is changed.</p>
<a href="./09_RRMM_NMA_Replication/01_Multinomial_NMA_Replication.qmd" class="stretched-link">View the replication &rarr;</a>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.card .h-100 .shadow-sm}

<h3 class="card-title">NICE TA1092 (Pembro) Case Study</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Mock Case — Extrapolation Audit & Spline Sensitivity</h6>
<p class="card-text">An EAG-style forensic audit of survival extrapolations (standard parametric vs. flexible splines), treatment-effect waning (5-7 years), and curve-crossing capping, using Guyot-reconstructed patient-level data.</p>
<a href="./07_TA1092_Pembro_ endometrial cancer/TA1092_Pembro_Endometrial_EAG_Case.qmd" class="stretched-link">View Case Study &rarr;</a>

:::

::: {.card .h-100 .shadow-sm}
::: {.card-body}
<h3 class="card-title">NICE TA975 (CAR-T) Case Study</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Full Submission Replication</h6>
<p class="card-text">A complete end-to-end reconstruction of a CAR-T therapy appraisal (Tisagenlecleucel). Features state-transition modeling, parametric survival fitting, and ICER calculations via Patient Access Schemes (PAS).</p>
<a href="./05_TA975_CAR-T_Case/TA975_Mock_Case.qmd" class="stretched-link">View Case Study &rarr;</a>

::: {.card-body}
<h3 class="card-title">ML-NMR: AML Population Alignment (TA1013)</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Mock Case — Population Alignment & Synthesis</h6>
<p class="card-text">A synthetic-data deep dive into Multilevel Network Meta-Regression. Solves the "Extrapolation Gap" using 64-point Sobol integration and Cholesky decomposition to bridge IPD and AgD seamlessly in a Bayesian framework.</p>
<a href="./03_Bayesian_NMA_Reconstruction/MLNMR_Flagship_Case.qmd" class="stretched-link">View ML-NMR Report &rarr;</a>

<h3 class="card-title">RWE External Control Arm: R/R DLBCL</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Mock Case — Doubly Robust Causal Inference Pipeline</h6>
<p class="card-text">A synthetic-data methodological showcase of External Control Arm construction for a fictional NICE appraisal. Implements IPTW, TMLE (doubly robust estimation), and E-value sensitivity analysis — aligned with the NICE RWE Framework (2022).</p>
<a href="./02_RWE_Causal_Inference_Pipeline/RWE_Mock_Case_DLBCL.qmd" class="stretched-link">View Case Study &rarr;</a>

<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Mock Case — Treatment Effect Waning & Recursive Hazard Chaining</h6>

## 💊 Market Access Decision Tools

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.card .h-100 .shadow-sm}
::: {.card-body}
<h3 class="card-title">Rebuilding a Published Budget Impact Model</h3>
<h6 class="card-subtitle text-muted mb-2">Venetoclax in AML — a replication of Palacios et al. 2024 (<em>PLoS One</em>, CC-BY)</h6>
<p class="card-text">A three-year budget impact model for venetoclax combinations in acute myeloid leukaemia, reconstructed from Palacios et al. (<em>PLoS One</em> 2024, CC-BY) rather than restated: epidemiology funnel, market share in both worlds, six cost components built from published quantities, and a one-way sensitivity analysis run on the parameters the source itself varied. Every input names where it came from — a trial, the Delphi panel, a national price list, or an explicit assumption — and the year-3 result reconciles to within 0.1% of the published figure under both payer perspectives.</p>
<p class="card-text"><small class="text-muted">A working deliverable would be an Excel workbook; this page exists to make the structure and its judgements visible.</small></p>
<a href="./06_Market_Access_Decision_Tools/01_Interactive_Budget_Impact_Model.qmd" class="stretched-link">Open the model &rarr;</a>
:::
